title: Node.js Minimum Version Raised to 20
description: CAP Node.js v9 requires Node.js 20 as the minimum supported runtime. Node.js 22 (LTS) is recommended. Projects running on Node.js 18 or older will break.

admin: Ensure all environments (development, CI/CD, production) are running Node.js version 20 or higher before upgrading to cds 9.
For new environments, use Node.js 22 LTS as the recommended version.
developer: Update `.nvmrc` to `20` or `22`.
Update the `engines` field in `package.json`: `"engines": { "node": ">=20" }`.
Update all Dockerfile base images to `node:20` or `node:22`.
Update CI/CD pipeline node setup steps accordingly.

title: Upgrade @sap/cds to Version 9
description: @sap/cds 7 is end of life and no longer patched. Version 8 continues to receive patches, but upgrading to version 9 is required to access the new features and fixes covered in this guide. Using @sap/cds 7 or lower now causes CLI errors at startup.

admin: Projects still running @sap/cds 7 must be upgraded immediately — no further security or bug fixes are provided for version 7.
Contact the development team to plan and execute the upgrade.
developer: Run `npm install @sap/cds@9`.
Verify startup succeeds and resolve any other changes listed in this guide.

title: Upgrade @sap/cds-dk to Version 9
description: @sap/cds-dk (the CAP development kit, providing the `cds` CLI) should be upgraded to version 9 in lock-step with @sap/cds. It is typically installed globally. A mismatched major version between cds and cds-dk can cause CLI errors and unexpected build behaviour.

admin: No direct action required from administrators. Ask the development team to update the global cds-dk installation.
developer: Run `npm install -g @sap/cds-dk@9`.
Confirm `cds version` reports version 9.

title: Upgrade @sap/cds-compiler to Version 6
description: @sap/cds-compiler 4 is end of life. @sap/cds 9 ships with cds-compiler 6 as a peer dependency. If cds-compiler is pinned separately in your project, it must be updated to version 6 to avoid version conflicts and compiler errors.

admin: No direct action required from administrators. Ask the development team to update the dependency.
developer: If @sap/cds-compiler is explicitly pinned in package.json, run `npm install @sap/cds-compiler@6`.
If it is only a transitive dependency of @sap/cds, no action is needed — it will be resolved automatically.

title: CAP Java 2.10 Reaches End of Life
description: CAP Java (cds-services / cds4j-api) version 2.10 is no longer patched. Projects must upgrade to CAP Java 4.0 for continued support.

admin: Update the CAP Java BOM version in your pom.xml to 4.0.x before the next deployment. No security patches will be delivered for version 2.10.
Schedule the upgrade with your development team.
developer: Update the Maven BOM `com.sap.cds:cds-services-bom` to version `4.0.x` in `pom.xml`.
Follow the full Java migration guide at https://cap.cloud.sap/docs/java/migration#three-to-four.

title: Transactional Event Queues Enabled by Default
description: The transactional event queue feature (evolution of the persistent outbox) is now active by default in both Node.js and Java. A new database table `cds.outbox.Messages` must be deployed. If the persistent outbox was not previously used, skipping deployment will cause runtime failures.

admin: A database deployment is required after upgrading to cds 9 / CAP Java 4. The new `cds.outbox.Messages` table must be created before the application starts.
If event queues are causing issues, ask a developer to temporarily disable them by setting `cds.requires.queue = false` in the project configuration.
developer: Run a full database deployment after upgrading — the new `cds.outbox.Messages` table must exist.
To temporarily opt out, set `cds.requires.queue = false` in `package.json` (Node.js) or `application.properties` (Java). Remove this setting once deployment is complete.
The old `cds.outboxed(srv)` is kept as a synonym for the new `cds.queued(srv)`.
The table name remains `cds.outbox.Messages` for compatibility.

title: Association to Many Without ON Condition Now an Error
description: `Association to many` without an ON condition was previously silently compiled as a managed `to one` association, generating foreign keys. It is now treated as unspecified, causing a compiler error. Existing models with this pattern must be fixed before deployment.

admin: After the development team fixes the data model, a schema migration/deployment is required. The spurious foreign key column generated by the old behavior may need to be removed from the database.
developer: Search for `Association to many` without an ON condition in all `.cds` files.
If you intended `to many`: add an ON condition — e.g. `books: Association to many Books on books.author = $self;`.
If you intended a managed `to one`: remove the `many` — e.g. `book: Association to Books;`.
If intentionally unspecified: ensure the entity is not deployed to the database and implement a custom handler.
Run `cds build` to verify no compiler errors remain.

title: $now Maps to Transaction Time Instead of current_timestamp
description: `$now` in CDS models now translates to `session_context($now)` (CAP-pinned UTC transaction time) instead of `current_timestamp` (database-server time). Exception: in `default` clauses, `$now` still maps to `current_timestamp`. This can affect stored timestamp values.

admin: Verify that timestamp-dependent data and reports are not affected by the switch from database-server time to CAP-pinned UTC transaction time.
Check any scheduled jobs or integrations that compare or sort by timestamp fields.
developer: If you require the old database-server time behavior, replace `$now` with `current_timestamp` explicitly in your CDS model definitions.
Views using `$now` will be regenerated — plan a redeployment.

title: != Operator Changed to Two-Valued Logic
description: The `!=` operator now uses two-valued Boolean logic (always `true` or `false`, never `null`). Previously it had SQL three-valued logic where comparing with `null` yielded `null`. This can silently change query results where null values are involved.

admin: Test all query-heavy functionality where null values may exist in filtered fields after upgrading.
developer: Review all CDS model filters, annotations with expression values, and CQN queries using `!=`.
If three-valued SQL logic is required, switch to `<>` instead.
Note: the `==` operator also follows two-valued logic (equivalent to `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM`).

title: @cds.persistence.journal Propagates to Generated .texts and Child Entities
description: When an entity is annotated with `@cds.persistence.journal`, its compiler-generated `.texts` entities and composition child entities now inherit this annotation. These tables will be deployed via `.hdbmigrationtable` instead of `.hdbtable`. Undeploy the `.hdbtable` and deploy `.hdbmigrationtable` in the same HDI deployment step to avoid data loss.

admin: Coordinate the migration deployment carefully with the development team — dropping `.hdbtable` and creating `.hdbmigrationtable` must happen in the same HDI deployment to avoid data loss.
Schedule a deployment window for this change.
developer: If you do NOT want child/text entities to inherit the annotation, explicitly annotate them with `@cds.persistence.journal: false`, e.g. `annotate Books.chapters with @cds.persistence.journal: false;`.
Plan and execute the migration deployment in a single HDI deployment step — undeploy `.hdbtable` and deploy `.hdbmigrationtable` together.

title: hdbcds SAP HANA Deploy Format Removed
description: The `hdbcds` deploy format for SAP HANA was deprecated in cds 8 and is now completely removed. Projects still using this format will fail to deploy. The replacement is the `hdbtable` format (default). Not relevant for SAP HANA Cloud.

admin: Migration from `.hdbcds` to `.hdbtable` requires a planned schema migration. Schedule a maintenance window with the development team.
developer: Follow the migration guide at https://cap.cloud.sap/docs/cds/compiler/hdbcds-to-hdbtable.
Switch the deploy format to `hdbtable` in your project configuration.
Run the schema migration as documented.

title: Native HANA Associations No Longer Generated
description: CDS associations are no longer reflected as native HANA `WITH ASSOCIATIONS` clauses in tables and views. This reduces ongoing deployment times, but the first deployment after upgrading to cds 9 will be longer than usual as every entity with associations is touched.

admin: Plan for a longer-than-normal first deployment after upgrading to cds 9. Subsequent deployments will be faster.
Ensure sufficient deployment window time for the initial migration.
developer: No action required for most projects — the change is automatic.
If native HANA associations are required by custom native HANA objects, re-enable with `cds.sql.native_hana_associations: true` in your config.

title: req.params Always Returns Array of Objects
description: `req.params` now always returns an array of plain objects (e.g. `[{ ID: 101 }]`), even for entities with a single key. Previously a single-key entity returned the primitive value directly (e.g. `101`). Any custom handler code accessing `req.params[0]` as a scalar will break.

admin: No action required from administrators. Ask developers to review and update custom handler code.
developer: Update all custom handlers that access `req.params`. Change `const id = req.params[0]` to `const { ID } = req.params[0]`.
To temporarily opt out while fixing: set `cds.features.consistent_params = false` in your config.
Search for all usages: `grep -rn 'req.params' . --include='*.js' --include='*.ts'`

title: @requires Annotation Now Enforced for Local Service Calls
description: Local (in-process) calls to application services that do not satisfy the service's `@requires` annotation are now rejected with a 403. Previously, local calls bypassed service-level authorization. This can break internal service-to-service calls within the same process.

admin: No direct action required from administrators. Ask developers to review internal service call authorization.
developer: Use the privileged user for trusted internal calls that should bypass `@requires`: https://cap.cloud.sap/docs/node.js/authentication#privileged-user.
To temporarily opt out while fixing: set `cds.features.service_level_restrictions = false` in your config.
Review all in-process service calls that could be affected.

title: @cap-js Database Packages Must Be Upgraded to v2
description: cds 9 requires major version 2 of all `@cap-js` database service packages (`@cap-js/sqlite`, `@cap-js/hana`, `@cap-js/postgres`). Additionally, violated unique constraints are no longer automatically mapped to `ENTITY_ALREADY_EXISTS` or `UNIQUE_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION` — they are now raw database errors.

admin: No direct action required from administrators. Ask developers to update database package versions.
developer: Run `npm install @cap-js/sqlite@2` and/or `npm install @cap-js/hana@2` and/or `npm install @cap-js/postgres@2` as applicable.

Review any custom error handling code that relied on `ENTITY_ALREADY_EXISTS` or `UNIQUE_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION` error codes for unique constraint violations — these must now inspect raw database errors.

title: Legacy Built-in Database Services Removed
description: The old built-in database services, deprecated since cds 8, are completely removed. Projects must use the `@cap-js/*` database service packages.

admin: No direct action required from administrators. Ask developers to update dependencies.
developer: Install the appropriate `@cap-js` database package: `npm install @cap-js/sqlite`, `npm install @cap-js/hana`, or `npm install @cap-js/postgres`.
See https://github.com/cap-js/cds-dbs for details.

title: @sap/cds-hana Package Removed — Replace with @cap-js/hana
description: The `@sap/cds-hana` package has been removed. The replacement is `@cap-js/hana`.

admin: No direct action required from administrators. Ask developers to update the dependency.
developer: Run `npm rm @sap/cds-hana && npm add @cap-js/hana`.
Update any explicit imports of `@sap/cds-hana` in code to `@cap-js/hana`.

title: Support for SAP Cloud SDK v3 Removed
description: CAP Node.js no longer supports SAP Cloud SDK v3. The minimum required version is v4. Projects using the Cloud SDK for remote service calls or integrations must upgrade.

admin: No direct action required from administrators. Ask developers to upgrade the SAP Cloud SDK.
developer: Upgrade to `@sap-cloud-sdk` v4 following the V4 Upgrade Guide: https://github.com/SAP/cloud-sdk-js/blob/main/V4-Upgrade-Guide.md.

title: Support for @sap/xssec v3 Removed
description: CAP Node.js no longer supports `@sap/xssec` v3. The security library must be upgraded to v4.

admin: No direct action required from administrators. Ask developers to upgrade the security library.
developer: Run `npm install @sap/xssec@4`.
Review the xssec v4 changelog for any API-level breaking changes.

title: cds.test Moved to Separate Package @cap-js/cds-test
description: The CAP Node.js test support library has been extracted to a separate open-source package `@cap-js/cds-test`. Tests using `cds.test` will fail unless the new package is installed. The new package bundles `axios`, `chai`, `chai-subset`, and `chai-as-promised` — these no longer need to be managed separately.

admin: No action required from administrators.
developer: Run `npm add -D @cap-js/cds-test`.
Run `npm rm axios chai chai-subset chai-as-promised` to remove now-redundant dependencies.
Update any test files that import directly from the old location.

autoFix.script: npm add -D @cap-js/cds-test && npm rm axios chai chai-subset chai-as-promised

title: PATCH No Longer Upserts by Default
description: In cds 8, PATCH and PUT both created the resource if it didn't exist. In cds 9, this is split into separate flags. `patch_as_upsert` now defaults to `false`, meaning PATCH no longer creates missing resources. Code relying on PATCH creating a missing resource will now get a 404.

admin: No direct action required from administrators. Ask developers to review API behavior changes.
developer: If PATCH-as-upsert is needed, set `cds.runtime.patch_as_upsert = true` in your config.
Remove any references to the old `cds.runtime.allow_upsert`.
Review code and tests that assume PATCH creates missing resources — these will now get a 404.

title: No Locale Fallback for Requests Without Accept-Language Header
description: `cds.context.locale` no longer falls back to the configured default language when no `Accept-Language` header is present (typical for technical/API calls). Data will be un-localized for such requests. Applications relying on default-language localization for technical API consumers will be affected.

admin: Verify that API consumers (integrations, batch jobs) that do not send an `Accept-Language` header still receive the expected data.
developer: Have API consumers send an explicit `Accept-Language` header if default-language content is required.
To temporarily restore the old behavior: set `cds.features.locale_fallback = true` in your config.

title: INSERT.as() Query Builder Method Removed
description: The `INSERT.as` method has been removed from the CDS query builder API.

admin: No action required from administrators.
developer: Replace `INSERT.as(...)` with `INSERT.entries(...)` or `INSERT.from(...)` as documented in the CDS Query Language reference.

title: srv.impl() and srv.with() Methods Removed
description: The `srv.impl()` and `srv.with()` methods for registering service implementations have been removed.

admin: No action required from administrators.
developer: Replace all usages of `srv.impl(...)` and `srv.with(...)` with `srv.prepend(...)` as documented in the Node.js core services reference.

title: cds.mtx Configuration Namespace and Legacy Extensibility Keys Removed
description: The `cds.mtx` configuration block is no longer supported. Additionally, legacy extensibility configuration keys (`entity-whitelist`, `service-whitelist`, `namespace-blacklist`) will now cause a hard error at startup.

admin: Update all environment configurations that reference `cds.mtx` — these will cause the application to fail at startup.
Coordinate with the development team to identify replacement configuration keys.
developer: Migrate from `cds.mtx` to the Extensibility Service Configuration namespace: https://cap.cloud.sap/docs/guides/multitenancy/mtxs#extensibility-config.
Remove any `entity-whitelist`, `service-whitelist`, or `namespace-blacklist` entries from configuration.

title: ESLint 9 Required for @sap/eslint-plugin-cds
description: `@sap/eslint-plugin-cds` v4 requires ESLint 9. ESLint 8 configurations will not work. Additionally, `cds lint` no longer bundles `eslint` — it must be installed as an explicit devDependency.

admin: No action required from administrators.
developer: Run `npm add -D eslint`.
Migrate ESLint configuration from v8 format to v9 flat config format: https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/migrate-to-9.0.0.
Update `@sap/eslint-plugin-cds` to v4.

title: Java: Deep Authorization Checks Enabled by Default
description: Three advanced instance-based authorization features are now enabled by default in CAP Java 4: (1) `authorization.deep` checks authorizations deeply through associations, (2) `rejectSelectedUnauthorizedEntity` returns 403 instead of 404 for unauthorized access, (3) `checkInputData` validates authorization on write payloads. Previously-passing requests may now be rejected.

admin: Test all authorization-sensitive operations thoroughly before upgrading in production.
Users or roles that previously could access nested data without explicit authorization may now receive 403 errors.
Update role assignments and inform end users if error messages change (404 → 403 for unauthorized access).
developer: Review all CDS service and entity definitions for deep associations — ensure `@requires` and `@restrict` annotations correctly cover all navigation paths.
Re-test all CREATE/UPDATE/UPSERT operations for entities with instance-based `@restrict` conditions.
To pre-test in cds-services 3.10.x, enable the flags manually before upgrading.

If needed, temporarily disable individual features: `cds.security.authorization.deep.enabled=false`, `cds.security.authorization.instanceBased.rejectSelectedUnauthorizedEntity.enabled=false`, `cds.security.authorization.instanceBased.checkInputData.enabled=false`.
Refer to https://cap.cloud.sap/docs/guides/security/authorization#deep-auth.

title: Java: Unstructured String Messaging Support Removed
description: The `cds.messaging.services.<key>.structured` property (which when `false` allowed raw string messages) is fully removed. MessagingService now always uses structured Map-based messages. The APIs `MessagingService.emit(String, String)` and `TopicMessageEventContext.getData()` are removed. Incoming unstructured strings are wrapped as `Map.of("message", <theString>)`.

admin: Remove the `cds.messaging.services.<key>.structured` property from all environment configurations.
Coordinate with teams that publish or consume raw string messages via the messaging service.
developer: **Sending:** Replace `messagingService.emit("myTopic", "text")` with `messagingService.emit("myTopic", Map.of("message", "text"))`.
**Receiving:** Replace `String msg = context.getData()` with `String msg = (String) context.getDataMap().get("message")`.
Remove `cds.messaging.services.<key>.structured=false` from all configuration files.
CDS-modelled events are unaffected.

title: Java: cds-feature-event-hub Moved to Open-Source
description: The built-in `cds-feature-event-hub` Maven artifact has been removed from the CAP Java release train. Its successor is the open-source CDS Plugin for SAP Cloud Application Event Hub (https://github.com/cap-java/cds-feature-event-hub), which uses the same Maven coordinates but starts at version 4.0.0.

admin: Confirm that the new open-source plugin version is approved for use in your organisation (open-source license review).
Ensure deployment pipelines can resolve the new artifact from Maven Central or your internal repository.
developer: No `pom.xml` coordinate change is needed — group ID and artifact ID are unchanged.
Ensure version `4.0.0+` of `cds-feature-event-hub` is available in your Maven repository.
Review the open-source project changelog at https://github.com/cap-java/cds-feature-event-hub for any API differences.

title: Java: Runtime Views Default to CTE Mode
description: The `cds.sql.runtimeView.mode` property changed default from `resolve` to `cte`. Runtime views are now translated into SQL Common Table Expressions by default. This may change query plans and performance characteristics.

admin: After upgrading, monitor application performance and run integration tests against the target database.
CTE-based queries may perform differently on HANA, PostgreSQL, H2, or SQLite.
developer: Run integration tests for all queries involving CDS runtime views.
If the old `resolve` behavior is required, set `cds.sql.runtimeView.mode=resolve` in `application.properties`.
Refer to https://cap.cloud.sap/docs/java/working-with-cql/query-execution#runtimeviews.

title: Java: OData V4 Responses Always Streamed — buffered Option Removed
description: The configuration property `cds.odataV4.serializer.buffered` has been removed. OData V4 responses are now always streamed. Streamed responses do not include a `Content-Length` header.

admin: Remove the property from all configuration sources.
Verify that downstream clients and API gateways are compatible with streaming OData V4 responses (no `Content-Length` header).
developer: Remove `cds.odataV4.serializer.buffered` from all configuration files.
Test OData V4 endpoints, especially for large result sets, to confirm streaming works correctly end-to-end.

title: Java: Subscription Manager clientCertificateHeader Property Moved
description: The property `cds.multiTenancy.subscriptionManager.clientCertificateHeader` has been removed. Replace it with `cds.security.authentication.clientCertificateHeader`.

admin: Update all deployment configurations to replace `cds.multiTenancy.subscriptionManager.clientCertificateHeader` with `cds.security.authentication.clientCertificateHeader`.
developer: Replace `cds.multiTenancy.subscriptionManager.clientCertificateHeader=<value>` with `cds.security.authentication.clientCertificateHeader=<value>` in all configuration files.

title: Java: CqnSearchPredicate Class Removed
description: The class `com.sap.cds.ql.cqn.CqnSearchPredicate` has been removed. It was deprecated in CAP Java 3.x in favour of `CqnSearchTermPredicate`. Projects using this class will fail to compile.

admin: No operational action required. Ask developers to fix the compilation error before deployment.
developer: Replace all usages of `com.sap.cds.ql.cqn.CqnSearchPredicate` with `com.sap.cds.ql.cqn.CqnSearchTermPredicate`.
Update all imports accordingly.
The project will fail to compile until this is fixed.

title: Java: Modifier.search(String) Method Removed
description: The deprecated method `com.sap.cds.ql.cqn.Modifier.search(String term)` has been removed. The replacement is `searchTerm(CqnSearchTermPredicate)`.

admin: No operational action required. Ask developers to fix the compilation error before deployment.
developer: Replace calls to `modifier.search("term")` with `modifier.searchTerm(CqnSearchTermPredicate)`.
Construct a `CqnSearchTermPredicate` using the appropriate builder from the `CQL` API.
The project will fail to compile until this is fixed.

title: Java: cds-maven-plugin generate excludes Default Changed
description: The `excludes` parameter of the `cds-maven-plugin` `generate` goal changed default from `"localized.**"` to `null`. Localized entity POJO classes will now be generated by default. Projects may see new unexpected generated classes.

admin: No operational action required.
developer: If you do not want POJO classes for localized entities to be generated, explicitly add `<excludes>localized.**</excludes>` to the `generate` goal configuration in `pom.xml`.
Review generated sources after upgrading to confirm no compilation conflicts with newly generated localized classes.

title: Java: sharedInterfaces and uniqueEventContexts Removed from cds-maven-plugin
description: The `sharedInterfaces` and `uniqueEventContexts` properties of the `cds-maven-plugin` `generate` goal have been removed (they were deprecated in CAP Java 3.x with defaults of `true`). Any explicit configuration of these properties must be removed.

admin: No operational action required.
developer: Remove any `<sharedInterfaces>` and `<uniqueEventContexts>` configuration from the `cds-maven-plugin` `generate` goal in `pom.xml`.
The behaviour is now always equivalent to `true` for both.
